English Language.question: 1) ‘To leave someone in the lurch’ means -
English Language.option1: ক) To come to compromise with someone
English Language.option2: খ) Constant source of annoyance to someone
English Language.option3: গ) To put someone at ease
English Language.option4: ঘ) To desert someone in his difficulties
English Language.option5: ঙ) to leave someone in occasion
English Language.exp:
To leave someone in the lurch: to leave someone abruptly and without assistance or support when they are in a difficult situation.
Example: he left you in the lurch when you needed him most.
Source: Oxford dictionary

English Language.question: 2) ‘to hit the nail on the head’ means -
English Language.option1: ক) To do the right thing
English Language.option3: গ) To announce one's fixed views
English Language.option4: ঘ) To teach someone a lesson
English Language.option5: ঙ) To get attention from someone
English Language.exp:
“to hit the nail on the head” means to say something that is exactly right or completely true.
Example: With regard to the gentleman’s comments, I think he has hit the nail right on the head.
Source: www.macmillandictionary.com/

English Language.question: 3) The expression ‘To cry wolf’ means
English Language.exp: English idiom ''to cry wolf'', defined as ''to give a false alarm'' in Brewer's Dictionary of Phrase and Fable and glossed by the Oxford English Dictionary as meaning to make false claims, with the result that subsequent true claims are disbelieved.

English Language.question: 4) “To put one's hand to plough” means -
English Language.option1: ক) To take up agricultural farming
English Language.option3: গ) To get entangled into unnecessary things
English Language.option4: ঘ) Take interest in technical work
English Language.exp:
To put one's hand to plough: to begin or undertake a task
Source: collinsdictionary.com

English Language.question: ৫) The expression “to beg the question” means -
English Language.exp:
Beg the question
English meaning:
(of a fact or action) raise a point that has not been dealt with; invite an obvious question.
2. Assume the truth of an argument or proposition to be proved, without arguing it.

• Taken for granted - to believe that something is true without checking or thinking about it.

সুতরাং, বুঝা যাচ্ছে, beg the question এর অর্থ to take for granted।

English Language.question: 6) The expression “Tie the knot” means -
English Language.exp:
“Tie the knot” means To get married.
Example: So when are you two going to tie the knot?
Source: cambridge dictionary

English Language.question: 7) “by fits and starts” means -
English Language.exp:
by fits and starts: with irregular bursts of activity.
Example: The economy was recovering in fits and starts.
Source: Oxford dictionary

English Language.question:
8) Choose the meaning of the underline phrase:
Companies producing goods play to the gallery to boost their sales.
English Language.option2: খ) cater to the public taste
English Language.option3: গ) attempt to appeal to popular taste
English Language.option4: ঘ) depend upon the public for approval
English Language.option5: ঙ) to fool public with emotion
English Language.exp:
Play to the gallery means to do things that one thinks will be popular among many people instead of doing what one thinks is right.
Source: www.merriam-webster.com/

English Language.question: 9) The popularity of yesterday's superstar is <u>on the wane</u>.
English Language.exp:
“On the wane” means becoming weaker or less extensive.
Example: the epidemic was on the wane.
Source: Oxford dictionary

English Language.question: 10) The thief <u>took to his heels</u> when he saw a policeman on the beat.
English Language.option1: ক) had some pain in his heels
English Language.option3: গ) could not decide what to do
English Language.option5: ঙ) ran away from the scene
English Language.exp:
The expression “took to his heels” means to begin to run away.
Example: They took to their heels when they saw the policeman approaching.
Source: www.merriam-webster.com/

English Language.question: 11) The rebels <u>held out</u> for about a month.
English Language.exp:
hold out: to resist or survive in difficult circumstances.
Example: the troops held out against constant attacks.
Source: Oxford dictionary

English Language.question: 12) The prince did not <u>take after</u> the king.
English Language.exp:
take after: resemble a parent or ancestor.
Source: Oxford dictionary

English Language.question: 13) The secretary and the treasurer are <u>hand in glove</u> with each other.
English Language.exp:
hand in glove means working together, often to do something dishonest.
Example: It was rumoured at the time that some of the gangs were working hand in glove with the police.
Source: Cambridge dictionary

English Language.question: 14) I met him after a long time, but he gave me the <u>cold shoulder</u>.
English Language.exp:
cold shoulder: a show of intentional unfriendliness.
Example: the new England manager gave him the cold shoulder.
Source: oxford dictionary

English Language.question: 15) A Government run by a dictator is termed as
English Language.exp:
Autocracy means a system of government by one person with absolute power.
Example: the Grand Duchy of Tuscany was an autocracy.
Source: oxford dictionary

English Language.question: 16) One who comes into another country to live permanently is termed as
English Language.exp:
Emigration means to leave one's country to live in another. Immigration means one who comes into another country to live permanently. Migrating is to move, like birds in the winter.
If the sentence is looking at the point of departure, use emigrate. The point of arrival? Immigrants. Talking about the actual process of moving? Use migrate.
Source: vocabulary.com

English Language.question: 17) A person who is skilled in horsemanship is termed as
English Language.exp:
Equestrian means a rider or performer on horseback.
Example: three-time equestrian medal winner was Phillip Dutton.
Source: merriam-webster dictionary

English Language.question: 18) A doctor who specializes in diseases of the nose is termed as
English Language.exp:
A doctor who specializes in treating diseases and problems of the nose is called a Rhinologist.
Example: Endoscopic advances have provided rhinologists with excellent imaging.
Source: cambridge dictionary

English Language.question: 19) Place where birds are kept is termed as -
English Language.exp:
Aviary means a large cage (= area surrounded by wire or bars) or closed space in which birds are kept as pets.
Source: cambridge dictionary

English Language.question: 20) One who does not marry, especially as a religious obligation is termed as -
English Language.exp:
Celibate means abstaining from marriage and sexual relations, typically for religious reasons.
Example: a celibate priest.
Source: Oxford dictionary

English Language.question: 21) One who believes that all things and events in life are predetermined is a
English Language.exp:
Fatalist means someone who believes that people cannot change the way events will happen and that events, especially bad ones, cannot be avoided.
Example:It's wrong to take this fatalist's view of global warming.
Source: Oxford dictionary

English Language.question: 22) Bringing about gentle and painless death from incurable disease is termed as-
English Language.exp:
Euthanasia means the painless killing of a patient suffering from an incurable and painful disease or in an irreversible coma. Also called mercy killing.
Source: Oxford dictionary

English Language.question: 23) Words different in meaning but similar in sound is termed as
English Language.exp:
A homonym is a word that is said or spelled the same way as another word but has a different meaning. ''Write” and “right” is a good example of a pair of homonyms.
Source: vocabulary.com

English Language.question: 24) A traveller in a hot-air balloon, airship or other flying craft is termed as
English Language.exp:
An aeronaut is someone who flies an aircraft: a pilot. Originally, an aeronaut was specifically someone who flew a balloon.
Source: vocabulary.com

English Language.question: 25) A person with a strong desire to steal is termed as
English Language.exp: A person with kleptomania has a recurring drive to steal that he or she cannot resist, stealing items for the sake of stealing, not because they need or want the items, or because they cannot afford to buy them.

English Language.question:
(Q. 26 to 30) : Read the following passage and answer the questions given below in the context of the passage.
A well-dressed young man entered a big textile shop one evening. He was able to draw the attention of the salesmen who thought him rich and likely to make heavy purchases. He was shown the superior varieties of suit lengths and sarees. But after casually examining them, he kept moving to the next section, where readymade goods were being sold and further on to the hosiery section. By them, the salesmen had begun to doubt his intentions and drew the attention of the manager. The manager asked him what exactly he wanted and he replied that he wanted courteous treatment. He explained that he had come to the same shop in casual dress that morning and drawn little attention. His pride was hurt and he wanted to assert himself. He had come in good dress only to get decent treatment, not for getting any textiles. He left without making any purchase.

26) The young man was well-dressed because
English Language.option1: ক) it was his habit to dress well
English Language.option2: খ) it was his wedding day
English Language.option3: গ) he wanted to meet the manager of the shop
English Language.option4: ঘ) he wanted to impress the salesmen
English Language.exp:
The young man wore smart clothes to catch the eye of the salesmen.
(d) is the correct answer here.

English Language.question: 27) The salesman in the shop are described as people who pay attention to
English Language.option1: ক) only young men and women
English Language.exp:
The young man came to the shop in a casual dress and drew little attention as the salesman in the shop paid attention to wealthy customers.
(c) is the correct answer here.

English Language.question: 28) The young man moved away to the hosiery section because he
English Language.option1: ক) was not interested in purchasing anything
English Language.option2: খ) did not like the readymade clothes
English Language.exp:
The young man moved away to the hosiery section because his intention was not to purchase anything.
(a) is the correct answer here.

English Language.question: 29) The manager asked the young man what he wanted because -
English Language.option1: ক) he would give him exactly what he was looking for
English Language.option2: খ) the salesman had drawn his attention to the indifferent attitude of the young man
English Language.option3: গ) he thought they could do more business with him that way
English Language.option4: ঘ) he thought the visitor was dissatisfied
English Language.exp:
The salesman paid attention to the indifferent attitude of the young man, so the manager asked the young man what exactly he wanted.
(b) is the correct answer here.

English Language.question: 30) The young man left without making purchases because he
English Language.option2: খ) could not find any item of his choice
English Language.option3: গ) wanted to make a point about the indifferent attitude towards the casually dressed customers.
English Language.option4: ঘ) decided to come to make the purchases later on
English Language.exp:
The young man left without making purchases because he had come only to make a point about the indifferent attitude of the salesmen towards casually dressed customers.
(c) is the correct answer here.
